<p class="eyebrow">Experimental desktop builds</p>

# Download LinkEDA

LinkEDA is available as a native desktop application for macOS and Windows.
Choose the edition for your operating system and R setup. All builds are
experimental, so keep copies of important data and verify consequential
analyses from the exported R recipe.

## macOS {#download}

The current macOS build is **LinkEDA 0.0.119** for **Apple Silicon** (M1 or
newer) and **macOS 14 or later**. The two application installers place
`LinkEDA.app` in the Applications folder. Installing one application edition
replaces the other. If you already work in R or RStudio, you can instead
install the smaller R binary package in your personal R library.

The application and installer are not yet signed with an Apple Developer ID
or notarised. macOS may therefore ask you to confirm that you trust the
downloaded software. Use the files linked on this page and verify their
checksums when you need to confirm file integrity.

### macOS checksums

| File | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| Standalone installer | `5ff6efff69815e24604123c8e33d3c9e45b6236e9bba5e4829c83b0f3f613390` |
| System R installer | `64314541bd87d99a7062b39da445303dabf00a2fb826b20e68902965b8a3ca6c` |
| R binary package | `dccf4c03b27fcefa81e28becc558b2ea029b8058c3b741059d662f3d7b5286bf` |

### Install and start on macOS

1. Close LinkEDA if an older version is running.
2. Open the downloaded `.pkg` and complete the installer.
3. Open **LinkEDA** from the Applications folder.
4. If macOS says that it cannot verify the developer, close that message and
   open **System Settings > Privacy & Security**.
5. Scroll to **Security**, find the message saying that LinkEDA or its
   installer was blocked, and choose **Open Anyway** (or **Abrir igualmente**).
6. Authenticate with your password or Touch ID, then choose **Open** in the
   final confirmation. macOS normally asks for this approval only once for a
   downloaded build.

If the installer itself is blocked, complete steps 4--6 immediately after
trying to open the `.pkg`, then run it again. If the installer succeeds but
the application is blocked at its first launch, repeat the same steps for
`LinkEDA.app`. Control-clicking the file and choosing **Open** may also display
the approval directly. You do not need to disable Gatekeeper.

The standalone edition keeps its R runtime inside the application. The System
R edition requires an Apple Silicon build of R 4.6; it reports that requirement
at launch if a compatible R installation cannot be found.

### Install the R package on macOS

The R package is a precompiled macOS binary for Apple Silicon, R 4.6 and
macOS 14 or later. In R or the RStudio Console, install its required R packages
and then install LinkEDA directly from the release:

```r
install.packages(c(
  "digest", "effectsize", "statmod", "withr", "janitor",
  "later", "mice", "miceadds", "psych"
))

install.packages(
  "https://github.com/valerop/LinkEDA/releases/download/v0.0.119-macOS/LinkEDA_0.0.119.tgz",
  repos = NULL,
  type = "binary"
)

library(LinkEDA)
LinkEDA()
```

You can also download the `.tgz` first and select it in RStudio through
**Tools > Install Packages > Install from: Package Archive File**. Install the
required packages in the first command before selecting the archive. Features
that use optional R packages report what else is needed when you open them.

Both Windows installers create a **LinkEDA** shortcut on the desktop. Neither
requires Rtools, Visual Studio or Windows Developer Mode. Internet access is
required while the required R packages are installed.

### Windows checksums

| File | SHA-256 |
|---|---|
| Complete installer | `9427D998EEFB6028B9B671CF6C6DC5564F77856F8753A2DFA4622FEEF9591516` |
| Standard installer | `55AA9C5BD2019589ADE97863CF73FECEC784BCF8ECBA2CA10AF351E0F1301832` |

### Install and start on Windows

1. Close LinkEDA if an older version is running.
2. Double-click the downloaded installer.
3. Wait while it installs LinkEDA and the required R packages.
4. Open **LinkEDA** from the desktop shortcut.

Running a newer installer updates an existing installation; uninstalling the
previous version is not required. Windows may show a reputation warning because
the experimental installers are not code signed. Check the filename and
SHA-256 value before running the file.

## Start with data

The Welcome window can import a supported data file or open an included
example. The editions that use an installed R can also start from an R data
frame:

```r
library(LinkEDA)
LinkEDA(mtcars)
```

The standalone macOS and complete Windows editions run their own private R
session behind the desktop application.

## Report a problem

Report bugs through the [LinkEDA issue tracker on
GitHub](https://github.com/valerop/LinkEDA/issues). Include the LinkEDA version,
operating-system version, installer edition and the steps that triggered the
problem. Do not attach confidential data; use a small anonymous example when
data are needed to reproduce the problem.
